definitions.explanation: The oldest daughter in a family. Used in formal contexts such as family registers, introductions, and official documents.

examples.japanese: {私|わたし}は{三人|さんにん}{姉妹|しまい}の{長女|ちょうじょ}です。
examples.english: I am the eldest daughter of three sisters.

examples.japanese: {長女|ちょうじょ}が{今年|ことし}{小学校|しょうがっこう}に{入学|にゅうがく}する。
examples.english: Our eldest daughter starts elementary school this year.

examples.japanese: {長女|ちょうじょ}として{家族|かぞく}の{面倒|めんどう}を{見|み}る{責任|せきにん}を{感|かん}じていた。
examples.english: As the eldest daughter, she felt a responsibility to take care of the family.

notes:
Compound of {長|ちょう} (eldest/senior) + {女|じょ} (daughter/female).

Birth order terms in Japanese:
- {長女|ちょうじょ} (eldest daughter), {次女|じじょ} (second daughter), {三女|さんじょ} (third daughter)
- {長男|ちょうなん} (eldest son), {次男|じなん} (second son), {三男|さんなん} (third son)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {長女|ちょうじょ}として (as the eldest daughter)
- {長女|ちょうじょ}が{生|う}まれる (the first daughter is born)

USAGE NOTE:
In conversation, people often say {上|うえ}の{娘|むすめ} (older daughter) or {一番上|いちばんうえ}の{娘|むすめ} instead. {長女|ちょうじょ} sounds more formal.
